stemBlocks.value: Make w the subject of the formula P = 2(l + w) (the perimeter of a rectangle).
Think first: w sits inside a bracket that is multiplied by 2, so remove the 2 before touching the bracket.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p095-q06 from workbook page 95.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write it as a single fraction if preferred.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by 2, subtract l, then state w.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: w = (P − 2l)/2, which is the same as w = P/2 − l

whyThisWorks.value: The bracket is the last thing to be built when the formula is evaluated, so it is the first thing to be dismantled when you reverse the process. Dividing by 2 undoes the outer multiplication and leaves a simple sum, from which l is removed by subtraction.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing w = P − 2l, forgetting to divide P by 2.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing w = P − 2l, forgetting to divide P by 2.

commonErrors.misconception: Expanding to P = 2l + 2w and then dividing only the 2w term.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Expanding to P = 2l + 2w and then dividing only the 2w term.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing w = (P − l)/2 by subtracting l before dividing.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing w = (P − l)/2 by subtracting l before dividing.

examTip.value: Peel a formula like an onion: undo whatever is outermost first, and the inner terms come free without extra work.
